unit.why: A single anecdote: at the great wedding in Ustila a man's belongings are stolen and the Apter rav identifies the thief, Chaim, through a verse.

stories.start_quote: כתב לי ידי"נ הגאון החסיד אבד"ק פלונסק
stories.summary_en: At the great wedding in Ustila a man's belongings are stolen on the Sabbath; the Apter rav has him list the suspects in writing and picks out the one named Chaim, citing 'ובחרת בחיים' from the previous Sabbath's portion Nitzavim, and so it proved.

quotes: השיב בש"ק העבר פ׳ נצבים כתיב ובחרת בחיים
tags.why: The tzaddik identifies the thief supernaturally.

quotes: שהי' בעצמו באוסטילא על החתונה הגדולה
tags.why: A wedding is the setting of the events.

quotes: שנגנב לאחד כל מה שהי' לו באותו השבת
tags.why: The theft happens on the Sabbath, and the clue is the Sabbath Torah portion.

quotes: ולמחרתו בא לפני הגה"ח מאפטא המחותן
tags.why: The victim comes before the tzaddik with his request.
A witty play on the name Chaim and the verse.
The tzaddik applies a verse from the weekly portion.
The tzaddik's pronouncement is confirmed ('וכן הוי'), though it is a detection rather than a prediction.

quotes: שנגנב לאחד כל מה שהי' לו
tags.why: The story turns on a theft.

missing_concepts: name-based wordplay as a divinatory clue
